T-ORDER.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: discount then points then rounded tax, cap/no excess consumption, fully-discounted zero floor and FR multi-line rounding pass.

T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: expired/empty lots skipped, earliest-expiry-first partial and four-lot allocations match exact ledger balances; other customer untouched.

T-IDEM.evidence: 5/6: tax reconfiguration replay changes tax 1868 -> 7176 and total 11698 -> 17006 because quote is recomputed; other replay/mismatch/concurrent-key tests pass.

T-RACE.evidence: 1/4 frozen cases pass; other three stop at GET quote omitting points for zero-applied successful orders; supplemental all four races conserve the ledger.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: original lot IDs/expiry restored, mixed-expiry and all-expired shares forfeited, repeated cancellation does not restore twice; debit/cancel share a compatible boundary.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases: missing session 401, foreign spend and foreign cancellation 403/404 with unchanged ledgers; replay is authorized and supplemental changed-owner replay rejects 404.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen shipped/cancelled rejections pass; source checks pending within the same effective concurrency boundary as cancellation before fresh debit.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: injected now is used, expiry is exclusive at equality, and advancing to expiry selects the later lot.

T-FAIL.evidence: 3/3 frozen pricing failures are prevalidated; supplemental order publication rejection after native debit leaves [0,0,404] rather than [81,123,500], with no rollback.

T-EFF.evidence: 3/3 API budgets pass (fresh/next four calls, replay three, zero visible records); source redeem still scans/sorts global lots privately and uses a global transaction queue, not an index.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: T-ORDER 4/4: outward quote caps at discounted cents and rounds reduced-base tax; excess points are not actually removed, though the adapter receipt overcounts requestedPoints when room is capped.

2. Lots and clock.why: T-LOTS 2/2 and T-CLOCK 2/2: store redeem filters positive live lots at explicit now, sorts by expiry and mutates only selected customer lots.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: T-IDEM 5/6: transaction plus per-order lock prevents repeated debit/mismatch execution, but stores applied counts instead of the original quote, so tax reconfiguration changes replay.

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: Global ledger transaction conserves points in supplemental yielding races and order locks serialize cancel/redeem; however order publication is outside the ledger transaction and a supplemental orders.save failure leaves all 300 points debited.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: T-REVERSAL 4/4: original allocation IDs/expiries and reversed flag restore only live shares exactly once under compatible order/ledger locks.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: T-AUTH 3/3 and supplemental changed-owner replay 404: withCustomer plus owned-order checks precede spend, reversal and replay.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: T-PENDING 2/2: pending checked under the per-order lock shared by cancel; ledger lock protects the balance independently.

8. Efficiency.why: T-EFF 3/3 measures four calls/zero visible lot records fresh/next and three/zero replay, but redeem privately spreads/scans the global lot Map and sorts each request; global contention and orderApplied history scans prevent indexed efficiency.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: No redemption application use case: route holds the order workflow and adapter owns allocation/reversal rules; points-aware pricing is also in application rather than pure pricing domain.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Public rerun confirms all nine existing tests; terse report accurately describes added routes, ledger serialization and checks without claiming new acceptance tests or indexed efficiency; hidden replay weakness is not evidence of fabricated commands.

summary: Native serialized ledger is race-safe, but replay reprices, zero-point GET quotes omit applied amounts, publication is not atomic, and private full-history work is hidden by the API counter. Hidden 29/33; public rerun 9/9; functional 19/21, quality 5/9. No redaction-caused failures. See supplemental.json for uncounted conservation/failure/ownership evidence.
